title: Fermentation pH Drift Watch
dataSources: Fermentation telemetry (`brew:fermentation`), brew-day records (`brew:batch`), mash probes (`brew:mash`), keg pressure (`kegerator:pressure`), tap pours (`kegerator:pour`), brew-fridge duty logs (`brewfridge:compressor`), cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`), and line-cleaning events (`tapline:clean`).
app: Homebrewing telemetry from Tilt/iSpindel fermentation sensors, Brewfather batch exports, ESPHome mash and fridge probes, keg pressure sensors, tap flow meters, and cellar climate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation
| stats earliest(ph) as start_ph latest(ph) as current_ph by batch
| eval ph_drift=round(current_ph-start_ph,2)
| sort ph_drift
description: Measures how far fermentation pH has moved from batch start so you can spot stalled or off-track fermentations.
value: pH drift adds another lens beyond gravity and temperature, helping you catch batches that are behaving differently before flavor problems are obvious.
implementation: Ingest pH readings from fermentation probes or batch annotations and review batches with unusual movement from their opening pH.
visualization: Bar chart of pH drift by active batch.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Homebrewing, Beer & Wine — typical feeds: Fermentation gravity/temperature (`brew:fermentation`), kegerator pours (`kegerator:pour`), wine-cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `brew:fermentation`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=brew:fermentation`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Fermentation sensors (Tilt/iSpindel hydrometer, temperature), kegerator flow meters and scales, and wine-cellar climate sensors via MQTT and Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Ingest pH readings from fermentation probes or batch annotations and review batches with unusual movement from their opening pH.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "brew:fermentation", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Fermentation pH Drift Watch** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=brew:fermentation`) across the full search range. The `earliest, latest` aggregation groups by `batch`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `batch`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation
| stats earliest(ph) as start_ph latest(ph) as current_ph by batch
| eval ph_drift=round(current_ph-start_ph,2)
| sort ph_drift
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table batch
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.16.11: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Bar Chart Of Ph Drift By Active Batch (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `brew:fermentation` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
